I will do it the way I usually judge a year: start from what I did before, look at water, look at money, and not take big risks. I am 78, just two people at home, so I will not spread myself too thin on cotton because cotton needs more watching and more spraying. Wheat and maize are the main eating-and-selling crops here, and with well water I can keep them steadier, so I will put most land into wheat-maize and leave a smaller piece for cotton. If I am not sure, I would rather put a little more fertilizer than come up short and lose yield. Around here, when wheat looks weak in spring, people regret saving one bag of fertilizer, not using it. So I will keep the wheat-maize on 8.0 mu and cotton on 2.1 mu. For wheat, I will use a solid base dressing and then one topdressing when it turns green strong in spring, with about 18 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu, and I will water about 3 times if the year is normal. For summer maize after wheat, I will sow quickly, keep the stand full, use about 16 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu, and water about 2 times. For cotton, I will not chase fancy seed unless I saw others get a good stand, so I will use improved seed that people nearby have used well, give it about 14 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu, and watch insects closely because cotton can lose fast if I wait too long. I will plough the cotton land, and for wheat-maize land I will keep it simpler, rotary for wheat and no-tillage or quick direct seeding for maize after wheat harvest.
